financials.stated_by: Wolfspeed, Inc. management stated that cash, cash equivalents, short-term investments and operating cash flows should be sufficient for at least one year; no revolver amount or quantified runway was disclosed in the opened filing.

debt_events.summary: Wolfspeed, Inc. and Wolfspeed Texas LLC filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions in the Southern District of Texas to implement a prepackaged plan of reorganization.
The Bankruptcy Court confirmed the joint prepackaged Chapter 11 plan; Wolfspeed continued operating as a debtor-in-possession pending the effective date.

The plan became effective and Wolfspeed emerged from Chapter 11. The company said the restructuring reduced total debt by approximately 70%, extended maturities to 2030 and reduced annual cash interest expense by roughly 60%; the Epiq case page records the effective date.

Wolfspeed entered first supplemental indentures for the New 2L Non-Renesas Convertible Notes and New 2L Renesas Convertible Notes. The FY2026 filing also reports a private placement of 3,250,030 shares and pre-funded warrants for approximately $96.9 million gross proceeds.
Wolfspeed reported that it was in compliance with all covenants relating to its New Senior Secured Notes, New 2L Notes and 1.5L Convertible Notes as of the fiscal year-end.
The Epiq case page states that the remaining Wolfspeed Texas LLC Chapter 11 case was closed as of September 23, 2026; the related Wolfspeed, Inc. case is shown as closed.

distress_signals.summary: Wolfspeed disclosed a headcount-reduction and facility-closure/consolidation plan initiated in the first quarter of fiscal 2025, followed by two additional headcount-reduction plans during fiscal 2026; it also referenced closure-related charges and the closure of its Durham Fab.

The company underwent a court-supervised Chapter 11 restructuring, including a prepackaged plan, confirmation and emergence; this is a material historical distress signal even though the case subsequently became effective and was later closed.

ownership.value: Public company. Following the reorganization, Renesas received 16,852,372 shares of New Common Stock as of 2026-06-28 and a warrant for 4,943,555 additional shares; Renesas also has a right to designate one board member while holding more than 10% of New Common Stock. Existing equity holders received approximately 1,306,896 New Common Stock shares.

output.risk_rationale: Wolfspeed has material post-restructuring liquidity—$1.09 billion of cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments against $1.69 billion of debt—and management stated that liquidity should cover at least one year, with covenant compliance reported at 2026-06-28. Counterbalancing that improvement, the company remains loss-making with a reported $549.4 million LTM operating loss and only recently emerged from Chapter 11 after a roughly 70% debt reduction; additional headcount and facility actions indicate continuing operating pressure.
